answer: Because the tundra stake is held until the ferrous settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the nectar audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 41% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. A farm running 32 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
